text:
## Recommendation

Product effort should prioritize **usability**, specifically the excessive-ads problem (`usability.excessive_ads`) and the cluster of Premium-gated playback controls (`billing.features_behind_premium`, `usability.playback_controls_locked`). These combine high complaint volume and high severity, and usability as a topic carries the largest number of complaint/cancellation reviews in the dataset at 17 [F14] with a severity sum of 44 [F15].

## Evidence

- **usability.excessive_ads**: 7 complaints [C05], severity sum 16 [C06], mean severity 2.285714 [C07], priority score 16 [C08]. Customers describe ads as too frequent or too loud, with some saying the app is unusable without Premium. Representative reviews: "The ads are so loud :'(" [ab67a772-c3b7-42ba-9b80-8d21d3857018] and "that always plays adds instead of songs ...if want to enjoy music free without adds don't download this app .." [cf6166ae-d71a-4839-9add-088645ad3b78].

- **billing.features_behind_premium**: 3 complaints [C09], severity sum 9 [C10], mean severity 3.000000 [C11], priority score 9 [C12] — the highest mean severity among the top volume issues. Customers describe losing the ability to pick songs or skip freely. Representative review: "Why it requires premium just to play next music / to choose music ??" [ad730d1a-829a-4dc4-9561-7e1cd07e2c30].

- **usability.playback_controls_locked**: 2 complaints [C25], severity sum 6 [C26], mean severity 3.000000 [C27], priority score 6 [C28]. This overlaps thematically with the Premium-gating complaints, reinforcing that locked controls are a recurring pain point across both billing and usability topics.

- **other.general**: 16 complaints [C01], severity sum 33 [C02], mean severity 2.062500 [C03], priority score 33 [C04] — the single largest issue by volume and score, but it is a catch-all with no specific defect named. Representative reviews: "The update made the app useless ...." [45c561b9-cc47-4d80-95d3-f0d20bc84af3] and "Noob app" [2d5cdd20-3094-40a5-bc6e-653302b59b56]. Because this bucket is vague, it should not itself set the roadmap, but its size suggests many unplaceable complaints may actually relate to ads/controls frustration already captured above.

## Alternatives considered

- **Access**: `access.general` has only 2 complaints [C13] but severity sum 8 [C14] and mean severity 4.000000 [C15], the highest mean severity of any issue. Topic-level, access has 2 complaint/cancellation reviews [F24] and severity sum 8 [F25]. Volume is too low to prioritize over usability right now, though the high severity (e.g., "Will not except my password" [de0a9cdf-8974-48bc-802f-331228df4619]) means this should be watched — a rise in volume would change the ranking.

- **Playback**: `playback.app_crash_freeze` has 2 complaints [C17], severity sum 8 [C18], mean severity 4.000000 [C19]. Topic-level, playback has 5 complaint/cancellation reviews [F18] and severity sum 18 [F19]. Crashes are severe but low-volume; examples include "App is stuck on loading/logo screen" [66a29b3c-c14d-440e-b722-b23e0c99ae82]. If crash counts grow, this would warrant reprioritization.

- **Billing/support**: Beyond `billing.features_behind_premium`, `billing.update_removed_free_features` has 2 complaints [C21], severity sum 6 [C22]. Topic-level, billing has 5 complaint/cancellation reviews [F20] and severity sum 15 [F21] — lower volume than usability's 17 [F14] and 44 [F15]. Billing issues are real but smaller in scale than usability right now.

The top 3 issues account for 49.1 percent of ranked complaint memberships [F09], underscoring that focusing there addresses close to half of all ranked complaints.

## Limits

This analysis is based on a self-selected set of historical reviews, not a representative or random sample. There is no revenue, plan-tier, or confirmed churn data available; cancellation-intent reviews (10 of them [F06]) only indicate stated intent, not confirmed cancellation, and must not be treated as churn. Of 100 completed classifications [F02], 11 were flagged needs_review [F07], meaning some categorizations are uncertain. Verification checks (20 distinct texts [F10]) showed 100.0 percent topic agreement [F11] and 95.0 percent intent agreement [F12] with a mean severity difference of 0.2 levels [F13], but this reflects agreement between two models, not ground-truth accuracy. The `other.general` and `access.general` buckets are catch-alls for vague complaints and should not be used alone to justify specific engineering fixes.
